subject: Aaron Rodgers released by the Pittsburgh Steelers
title: Aaron Rodgers released: Why did the Steelers cut him? A public feud
answer: The Pittsburgh Steelers released quarterback Aaron Rodgers on Wednesday, Nov. 25, 2026, hours after he sharply criticized head coach Mike McCarthy on "The Pat McAfee Show." The team had benched him a day earlier, and he was placed on waivers, with the move made official on Thanksgiving, Nov. 26.
in_the_news: Rodgers, 42, had said 2026 would be his final NFL season, so the split may end his career. It also puts pressure on McCarthy, whose 6-4 Steelers host Denver on Friday with Mason Rudolph at quarterback.
body:
The break came fast. Late Tuesday, Nov. 24, the Steelers announced that Rodgers would be inactive for Friday's game against the Denver Broncos and that Mason Rudolph would start, NFL.com reported. That came hours after McCarthy had publicly backed Rodgers as his starter following a Week 11 loss in Philadelphia. In 10 starts, Rodgers had completed 220 of 361 passes for 2,241 yards, 16 touchdowns and six interceptions.

On Wednesday, Rodgers appeared on "The Pat McAfee Show" and said he had told McCarthy, "If you try and bench me or don't change the play calling then you should just release me." He also accused the coach of falling asleep in meetings and of breaking a halftime huddle against the Eagles by saying "1-2-3 Packers," and said he learned of the benching from tight end Pat Freiermuth. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported that the team had planned to keep Rodgers but changed course after the interview. At his press conference that afternoon, McCarthy said benching Rodgers was his decision, called the quarterback's demand an "ultimatum" that was outside his job description, and denied holding a grudge from their years together in Green Bay. He also said he had the full support of team leadership.

Key term — waivers: because the release came after the NFL trade deadline, Rodgers, a veteran, could not simply become a free agent. He was placed on waivers, a window in which any of the other 31 teams can claim him; during the season, priority goes to teams with the worst records. Claims are due by 4 p.m. ET on Thursday, Nov. 26. A team that claims him takes on the rest of his 2026 salary, about $8.6 million. If no team claims him, he becomes a free agent and can sign anywhere. Early reports suggested limited interest.

The feud has a long history. Rodgers played under McCarthy with the Green Bay Packers from 2006 through 2018, and the two reunited in Pittsburgh this season after McCarthy replaced Mike Tomlin, who stepped down in January 2026. Rodgers turns 43 next week. Whether he plays again depends on the waiver result and on whether a contender wants a veteran for the final weeks of the season.

faq.q: Who is the Steelers' quarterback now?
faq.a: Mason Rudolph is starting Friday's home game against the Denver Broncos on Nov. 27, 2026, at 3 p.m. ET on Prime Video.

faq.q: What did Aaron Rodgers say about Mike McCarthy?
faq.a: On "The Pat McAfee Show" on Nov. 25, he said he had told McCarthy to release him if he was benched or play-calling did not change, and accused the coach of falling asleep in meetings and saying "1-2-3 Packers" in a huddle. McCarthy called the demand an ultimatum and said benching him was his decision.
He had already said 2026 would be his final season. If no team claims him off waivers or signs him as a free agent, his Steelers game against the Eagles may have been his last.
No. Reports on Nov. 25 said the Steelers organization fully supports McCarthy and is not planning any immediate changes.
